subject: HorizonHealth MAP — Validation playbook & close sequencing
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@nexhealth.com>, Jason Miller <jmiller@horizonhealth.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HorizonHealth MAP — Validation playbook & close sequencing

Hi Emily / Jason —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together an initial validation playbook (attached) that ties acceptance tests to decision gates and a proposed close sequence. High level ask: can you confirm these success criteria and the timeline below so we can lock the pilot/canary dates?

Key acceptance buckets (draft):
- Functional correctness: model must pass the 30-case clinical prompt set with >= 92% match to SME baseline (exceptions documented).
- Latency SLO: 95th perc. inference latency < 220ms for typical 512-token requests under pilot load.
- Data controls: no PHI persisted outside customer VPC; audit log entries must include request id and model version.
- Stability: <1% error rate (5xx or timeouts) over a 48h window during pilot.
- Business validation: conversion uplift signal (end-to-end flow) consistent in A/B preliminary test window.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 1 (10/12): baseline data sampling + env prep.
- Week 2 (10/19): pilot canary (10k requests) — collect perf & quality metrics.
- Week 3 (10/26): evaluation window and SME review.
- Week 4 (11/02): go/no-go and close planning (SOW sign, procurement kick-off).

Attachments: Horizon_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones, owners, acceptance tests).

Can you confirm the latency SLO and procurement timing? If you want, Marissa can add the acceptance test checklist into your templated format.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@nexhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jason Miller <jmiller@horizonhealth.org>, procurement@horizonhealth.org
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonHealth MAP — Validation playbook & close sequencing

Sean —

Thanks for the clear playbook. I reviewed the document with our clinical leads and procurement team this morning. A few notes from our side:

1) Success criteria: clinical SME baseline is fine but we need a framing that allows for domain drift — can we add an "acceptable divergence" log for items flagged as "clinical nuance"? It should be a documented review path rather than an auto-fail.
2) Latency: 220ms p95 is reasonable for our interactive triage flow, but procurement will want a hard SLA only after GA. For the pilot we can accept an operational SLO with weekly reporting.
3) Data controls: please attach your SOC2 + encryption in transit/in-rest docs. Procurement asked specifically about key management (do you support customer-managed KMS?).

Procurement notes: we have an internal review on 10/21 and would like to have the SOW draft by 10/18 to slot legal review.

Attached: Horizon_Security_Addendum.docx (contains our current vendor checklist) — I'll also loop in our security lead if needed.

Emily
Emily Zhou
Director, Digital Experience
NexHealth (on behalf of Horizon Health)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@nexhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonHealth MAP — Validation playbook & close sequencing

Emily / Sean —

Thanks — I pulled Marissa-level detail into the acceptance checklist and added an "escalation rubric" for clinical nuance. Summary of concrete updates I propose to the MAP: 

A) Acceptance test definitions (pass/fail):
 - "Clinical match": SME adjudication on a 30-case set. Pass = >=92% exact intent/diagnosis match OR documented exception approved by SME within 3 business days.
 - "Latency": measured p95 under simulated pilot load (concurrency and token distribution in tab "LoadProfile"). Operational pass = p95 < 220ms; conditional pass if p95 between 220–300ms with mitigation plan and acceptance by EM.
 - "Data controls": evidence of KMS support (customer-managed or equivalent), audit log export sampling (3 requests) that include request id, model version, and truncated payload indicators.
 - "Stability": error rate <1% rolling 48h; emergency rollback plan documented in MAP.

B) Exit gates (suggested):
 - Gate 1 (Env ready): infra validated, KMS integrated, test keys rotated.
 - Gate 2 (Pilot green): acceptance tests run, SME sign-off or documented exception, SLA report delivered.
 - Gate 3 (Close): SOW signed, procurement approval, and a one-week smoke run in customer account.

C) Evidence artifacts: test reports CSV, SME adjudication notes (doc), latency traces (perf tool export), SOW draft.

I've also pushed a collaborative copy here: https://redwood.app/s/teams/horiz-4392/validation-playbook — feel free to comment. I'll attach a formal checklist to the MAP and can send the updated XLSX by EOD Thursday (10/08).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Jason Miller <jmiller@horizonhealth.org>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@nexhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.org
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonHealth MAP — Validation playbook & close sequencing

Sean / Emily —

Appreciate the draft. A couple procurement/security asks before we move the SOW to legal: 

- Please provide your SOC2 scope and latest report (Emily, you mentioned this).
- We need the SOW draft to include a clear indemnity clause and a 30-day data deletion guarantee after contract termination for pilot data.
- On performance: our internal infra team wants a 95th perc. latency target for 256-token interactive calls to be <200ms where feasible. If you can provide an empirical report from a representative run, that would be ideal.

I'll tentatively hold our internal review on 10/21 but we can move it if procurement needs more time. Attached: SOW-draft.pdf (template with our procurement redlines).

Thanks — Jason
Jason Miller
VP, Digital Ops
Horizon Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Miller <jmiller@horizonhealth.org>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@nexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, procurement@horizonhealth.org
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HorizonHealth MAP — Validation playbook & close sequencing

Jason / Emily —

Great feedback — short answers and next steps: 

1) SOC2 + security: attaching SOC2 summary and KMS capability matrix in separate message (we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS & GCP CMEK). We'll provide the scoped report under NDA by 10/22.
2) Latency reports: Marissa is preparing a 256-token representative run from our Dedicated infra with p95 figures (we expect ~180–210ms depending on concurrency). We'll share the perf export by 10/18.
3) SOW / procurement redlines: noted. Our legal team is ok to discuss the indemnity language; data deletion guarantee and audit logs are scoped in the draft SOW (we'll mark pilot-data deletion as a contractual clause). I'll ask our contracts lead to join the 10/21 review if needed.

Proposed next milestones: 
- 10/18: Redwood uploads perf export + updated MAP with checklist (Marissa).
- 10/21: Horizon internal procurement review (tentative).
- 10/26: Pilot canary start (subject to gate 1 completion).
- 11/02: Go/No-go meeting with decision owners.

If that sequencing works, I'll update the MAP and SOW tracker and send a single consolidated packet for legal. Thanks all — excited to get this into a pilot.

Best,
—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions
